mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Compare Team A's ratio of shots_on_target FOR to shots FOR under ALL_PRIOR versus RECENT_5 windows. Team A's shots FOR rises from ~12.1 (ALL_PRIOR) to ~14.0 (RECENT_5) while shots_on_target FOR stays flat at ~4.0, implying the conversion ratio compresses as volume increases. Test whether this decoupling (rising shots, flat on-target) is a persistent joint pattern across historical matches.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: As Team A's shot volume rises above its season baseline, shots_on_target rises less than proportionally — the on-target ratio is suppressed when shot volume is elevated.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: When Team A's shot volume rises in recent matches relative to its season average, its shots-on-target rate (shots_on_target / shots) does not rise proportionally, suggesting a saturation or decoupling between shot volume and shot quality that is not captured by either observable alone.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly tracking two distinct observables (shots and shots_on_target) and their ratio across two time windows; it cannot be reduced to either observable measured alone against a single band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team A concedes 0.667 goals in the first half and 0.889 in the second half (ALL_PRIOR), a second-half uplift of ~33%. Simultaneously, shots against Team A have risen sharply in RECENT_5 (16.4 vs 12.5 season average). Condition on whether elevated shots-against co-occurs with the second-half goal-concession uplift being larger than the competition's own first-half/second-half split, using half-level goal data.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team A's shots-against volume is elevated above its season baseline, its second-half goal concession rate rises more than its first-half rate — the second-half defensive vulnerability is amplified jointly with shot-volume pressure.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team A's second-half goal concession rate is disproportionately higher than its first-half concession rate relative to the competition norm, and this asymmetry co-occurs with Team A conceding more shots in recent matches — suggesting a joint relationship between defensive shot-volume allowed and second-half goal vulnerability.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This combines two distinct observables (shots against and goals against) across two within-match periods (first half vs second half), requiring a joint cross-observable, cross-period conditioning that is not reducible to a single observable with one band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team B's yellow_cards FOR rises from ~2.19 (ALL_PRIOR) to ~3.0 (RECENT_5) while fouls FOR stays near its season average (~12.4 ALL_PRIOR vs ~12.0 RECENT_5). Simultaneously, Team A commits more fouls away (~14.1) than at home (~12.8). Jointly condition on both teams' foul rates and the card-per-foul conversion ratio to test whether elevated card rates emerge from foul volume, foul-to-card conversion, or their interaction.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: Team B's card-per-foul conversion rate rises in recent matches independently of foul volume, and this elevated conversion co-occurs with Team A's higher away-foul tendency — jointly predicting elevated total match card volume beyond what either team's foul rate alone would suggest.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's yellow card production has spiked sharply in recent matches relative to its season average, while its foul rate has not risen proportionally — suggesting a joint relationship between foul volume and card conversion rate (cards per foul) that may interact with Team A's elevated foul production away from home.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This is a joint relationship between two distinct observables (fouls and yellow_cards) for two different teams simultaneously, with a cross-team asymmetry (Team A away foul rate vs Team B card conversion), not reducible to either observable alone with a single band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Team B's possession FOR drops ~5 percentage points away vs home, while Team A's possession is stable across venues. Simultaneously, Team A's corners FOR are stable across venues (~4.78 home vs ~4.78 away) but Team B's corners FOR are also stable (~4.83 home vs ~4.77 away). Test whether the joint condition of Team B playing away (possession-suppressed) combined with Team A's corner production creates a measurable asymmetry in total corner volume relative to when Team B plays at home.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When Team B plays away, its possession suppression is not accompanied by a proportional corner suppression, suggesting the possession-to-corner conversion relationship is non-linear and venue-asymmetric across the two teams jointly.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's possession advantage at home versus away is asymmetric: it holds ~51.6% at home but only ~46.2% away, while Team A's possession is nearly venue-invariant (~48.4% home, ~48.3% away). This creates a joint possession-venue interaction where the two teams' combined possession profiles shift substantially depending on which team is at home — and this possession shift may jointly co-vary with corner kick production differences across venues.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two distinct observables (possession and corner_kicks) across two teams simultaneously, with venue as a dimension that affects the two observables differently for each team — not reducible to one observable with one venue band.

mechanisms.conditioning_logic: Jointly condition on Team B's goals FOR split by half (first vs second) and Team A's goals AGAINST split by half (first vs second). Both point in the same direction: second half favors Team B's attack and disfavors Team A's defense. Test whether this joint half-level alignment (attacker's second-half uplift meeting defender's second-half vulnerability) is a persistent pattern historically across matches with similar half-level profiles.
mechanisms.expected_relationship_to_test: When an attacking team's second-half goal rate exceeds its first-half rate AND the defending team's second-half concession rate exceeds its first-half concession rate, total second-half goals in the match rise above what either team's individual half-level average would predict independently.
mechanisms.mechanism_statement: Team B's second-half goal scoring rate exceeds its first-half rate (~0.786 vs ~0.600), while Team A's second-half defensive record is weaker than its first-half record (~0.889 conceded vs ~0.667). This creates a joint cross-team, cross-half asymmetry: Team B's scoring profile peaks in the half where Team A's defensive profile is weakest — a structural alignment that is not captured by either team's half-level data in isolation.
mechanisms.why_not_baseline_equivalent: This requires jointly conditioning on two teams' goal observables simultaneously across two within-match periods, creating a cross-team, cross-half interaction that cannot be reduced to one team's observable with a single half-level band.
